articles.title: Image Compress Workflow: Reduce File Size Without Ruining Quality
articles.excerpt: Large images are one of the easiest ways to make a fast website feel slow. A single photo exported directly from a camera or design tool can outweigh the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript used to render the e…
articles.body: Large images are one of the easiest ways to make a fast website feel slow. A single photo exported directly from a camera or design tool can outweigh the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript used to render the entire page. An effective image compress workflow is not about pushing every file toward the lowest possible number. It is about removing data the visitor will never see while preserving the detail that makes the image useful. This guide walks through a repeatable process you can apply to blogs, product pages, portfolios, and documentation sites. TL;DR Resize before compressing. Match the file format to the image content. Judge quality at the actual display size. Deliver responsive variants and lazy-load only non-critical images.
articles.author: 王康

articles.title: Excel date functions: EDATE, EOMONTH, NETWORKDAYS, WORKDAY, DATEDIF
articles.excerpt: Contract renewals, payment terms, notice periods, probation end dates: a lot of office work is date arithmetic. Counting it out on a calendar works until a month has 31 days, a weekend gets in the way…
articles.body: Contract renewals, payment terms, notice periods, probation end dates: a lot of office work is date arithmetic. Counting it out on a calendar works until a month has 31 days, a weekend gets in the way, or a public holiday moves the deadline. Excel has a function for each of those cases. TL;DR: EDATE for "n months later", EOMONTH for month ends, NETWORKDAYS and WORKDAY for business days, WEEKDAY for the day number, DATEDIF for full years. All examples were calculated on a small date sheet in Excel for the web. The six functions EDATE: the same day, n months later. =EDATE(B2,6) gives the date six months after the contract date in B2 (a March 15 start lands on September 15). If you see a five-digit number instead of a date, change the cell's number format to Short Date .

articles.body: Our Go ingest service sits in front of smg-project/smg , the engine-agnostic Rust gateway that exposes OpenAI and Anthropic compatible APIs over vLLM, TRT-LLM, SGLang, TokenSpeed and hosted providers, with a gRPC pipeline and KV cache-aware routing. We adopted it as the single egress point for every provider so our application code stops carrying eight SDKs. Everything ahead of it is ours: tenant auth, prompt shaping, fan-out, rate limiting, and a worker pool. The worker pool is where we got hurt twice. Postmortem 1: the send that never returned The original pool was 64 goroutines reading from an unbuffered channel. Producers did ch <- job and moved on.

articles.title: Chats de IA borrados y privacidad en Android: ORISA avisa

articles.body: Los chats de IA borrados no desaparecen del todo del teléfono. La privacidad en Android enfrenta un hueco concreto: una herramienta forense llamada ORISA recuperó conversaciones eliminadas de asistentes que corren en el propio celular y las volvió a poner en marcha como una sesión nueva. El hallazgo lleva la firma de Georgia Tech. Borrar la conversación limpia la pantalla y el historial visible, pero fragmentos del intercambio quedan en la memoria de trabajo del equipo mientras el asistente sigue activo. ORISA rastrea esa memoria, junta los pedazos y reconstruye el contexto perdido. La diferencia importa porque los asistentes locales venden justo lo contrario a la nube: procesan en el teléfono, sin enviar cada pregunta a un servidor lejano.

articles.title: I verified a real x402 v2 quote in Python without connecting a wallet
articles.excerpt: One live HTTP 402, eighteen offline tests, zero charges. This is an educational demonstration of the public API operated by the same human owner as the client. The CLI is MIT licensed; using the paid…
articles.body: One live HTTP 402, eighteen offline tests, zero charges. This is an educational demonstration of the public API operated by the same human owner as the client. The CLI is MIT licensed; using the paid API is optional. If you have tried an x402 endpoint, you might have confused three very different outcomes: The server responds 402 Payment Required with a proposed price. A buyer authorizes a transfer, and funds settle on-chain. The server completes the paid request and returns the purchased result. These do not imply each other. I wanted a small Python tool that verifies step 1 and cannot silently perform step 2 . The live experiment On 20 October 2026, I ran a local, Python-standard-library-only CLI against an existing paid CSV preflight endpoint that our single-owner workflow operates.

articles.title: Four checks before shipping a password-reset email template
articles.excerpt: A password-reset email has a small job: help the intended recipient choose a new password without confusing them about what happened. The HTML is only one part of that job. “This link expires in 30 mi…
articles.body: A password-reset email has a small job: help the intended recipient choose a new password without confusing them about what happened. The HTML is only one part of that job. 1. Write the expiry once, then enforce it elsewhere “This link expires in 30 minutes” is a claim about your backend. Changing the email template does not change token validity. Pass the displayed lifetime from the same application configuration that controls expiry, and test that the values agree. Single-use enforcement belongs in the backend too. 2. Escape the URL, but also control its origin When substituting a URL into an HTML attribute, escape it for that context. Python's html.escape(url, quote=True) handles characters such as ampersands and quotation marks.

In an October 12, 2026 research post, Anthropic's Frontier Red Team described experiments with small models and inexpensive internet-connected devices. The headline risk is an AI-assisted worm that could adapt to unfamiliar hardware and spread without a data center. But the post does not report a real-world self-replicating worm in circulation.

articles.title: 8 Classic PlayStation Adventure Games that are Barely Playable Today
articles.excerpt: From Tomb Raider to Silent Hill, eight classic PlayStation games whose tank controls, cameras, or lost code make them hard to play today
articles.body: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

articles.excerpt: Brick by brick ... the truth is out there. You can now own a little piece of that with this 1,478-piece Lego set
articles.body: Millennials get a lot of flak for being overly nostalgic, but I don't think that's fair. When the modern-day world has nothing to offer us but AI slop, shrinkflation and a sad acceptance that we can't be bothered to do anything about global warming. It's easy to see why we yearn for the days of Pogs, the Backstreet Boys, and Saved by the Bell. One area that we definitely had it good in the 90s was sci-fi , when legendary shows like Star Trek: The Next Generation, Stargate SG-1, and — of course — The X-Files ruled our TV screens long before the age of streaming services . articles.title: Japan launches historic MMX sample-return mission to Mars' moon Phobos (video)
articles.excerpt: Japan just launched an epic mission to Mars' moons that could make history as the first spacecraft to return to Earth from the Red Planet — and it plans to come back with samples onboard.
articles.body: Japan's groundbreaking mission to Mars is officially underway, headed to the Red Planet's mysterious moons Phobos and Deimos for a historic sample-return attempt. The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launched today (Oct. 19) from Tanegashima Space Center in Japan, riding an H3 rocket that lifted off from Pad-2 at Tanegashima's Yoshinobu Launch Complex at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan on Oct. 20). The JAXA ( Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency )-led MMX mission is bound for Mars orbit, where it will study the planet's two moons, Phobos and Deimos.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 19, 2016: Europe's ExoMars orbiter and Schiaparelli lander arrive at Mars
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars orbiter and Schiaparelli arrived at Mars! Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars mission arrived at Mars ! ExoMars 2016 consists of the Trace Gas Orbiter and the Schiaparelli lander. The orbiter and lander traveled there together and separated on Oct. 16, three days before the orbiter entered orbit around Mars , and the lander touched down on the planet's surface. But something went wrong during the lander's descent, and it crashed into the ground. Schiaparelli did not survive the accident , but the Trace Gas Orbiter is still functional. It is currently circling the planet, looking for methane and other gases in the Martian atmosphere that could be evidence for possible biological activity.

articles.title: The moon is shrinking. 10,000 cracks on the lunar surface reveal by how much
articles.excerpt: One new study shows how much the moon has diminished over time.
articles.body: The moon is shrinking, and scientists are narrowing in on exactly how much our natural satellite has dwindled over the years. The moon is thought to have formed from a violent collision between a massive object and our young Earth roughly 4.5 billion years ago, and its interior is still gradually cooling off from this ancient collision. As it cools, the moon contracts, leading to a long, slow shrinking process . Now, in a new study, scientists think that they have figured out how much smaller the moon is actually getting. In this new study, scientists analyzing images snapped by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) have spotted over 10,000 young faults, or cracks across the moon's surface.
